question: What thermodynamic constraints govern physical learning machines, and can noisy classical or quantum activation switches, limit-cycle spiking elements, and single-photon kernels realize useful low-power learning primitives?

key_findings.claim: The paper offers a useful device-first vocabulary in which an activation function is the ensemble response of a stochastic physical switch, not a deterministic software primitive.
key_findings.evidence: A biased overdamped double well is coarse-grained to a two-state Markov process. Its binary output fluctuates, while the mean response is sigmoid-like; work, switching time, and heat are trajectory-dependent. The same formalism is extended to partially observed switches and low-temperature quantum-dot tunnelling monitored by a quantum point contact.

key_findings.claim: The perceptron constructions demonstrate qualitative learning only on NOT and XOR simulations, not an energy-efficient physical learner.
key_findings.evidence: The discrete scheme estimates a Bernoulli mean using 200 repeated samples per update and applies analytic gradient rules. Figures 15 and 18 show one average-error trajectory for hand-set initial parameters on two tiny logic tables. There is no fabricated device, measured work or heat, compute-normalized baseline, seed distribution, test split, larger task, scaling curve, or end-to-end energy accounting including sensing and feedback.

key_findings.claim: The central claim that energy dissipation and entropy change are proportional to learning rate is not established by the displayed derivation.
key_findings.evidence: Equations 89-92 calculate changes in mean internal energy and Shannon entropy of a two-state distribution, not dissipated heat or total entropy production. Moreover, from delta-E=2E0 delta-p1 and delta-error=-nT delta-p1, the identity is delta-E=-2 nT E0 delta-error; Equation 90 inserts an additional eta even though delta-error already contains eta through the update. Equation 92 similarly inserts eta again. The conclusion also conflates a vanishing parameter update at convergence with a thermodynamic optimum.

key_findings.claim: The two-state fluctuation calculation contains a state-hazard error that weakens later work identities.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 17 assigns the no-switch probability exp[-integral(mu+nu)dt] independently of the occupied state. For a two-state continuous-time chain, a trajectory initially in -1 has no-jump survival exp[-integral mu dt], while one initially in +1 has exp[-integral nu dt]; an unconditional survival is their initial-probability-weighted mixture. The printed expression instead treats both mutually exclusive outgoing hazards as simultaneously active. Equations 18-20 build on this simplification, and no numerical or trajectory-level verification is supplied.

key_findings.claim: The spiking section gives a plausible noise-power design intuition, but its learning architecture remains a proposal rather than a trained stochastic network.
key_findings.evidence: A Schmidt-trigger/oscillator model undergoes a Hopf bifurcation; phase diffusion decreases with limit-cycle radius while dissipation grows with radius squared. The post-synaptic leaky-integrate-and-fire element and rate code are illustrated with deterministic traces and chosen thresholds. The paper explicitly says SNN training is unsettled and does not optimize a multi-neuron noisy network, compare surrogate-gradient or STDP methods, or report classification accuracy and power.

key_findings.claim: The proposed single-photon kernel embedding is incorrectly normalized and does not demonstrate a computational or energy advantage.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 120 sets nu(t)=sum_j xi_j u_j(t) with xi_j in {+1,-1}, but orthonormality gives integral |nu|^2=N, not the unity asserted in Equation 121; a factor 1/sqrt(N) is missing. Consequently the claimed unit-probability parallel case and subsequent kernel scale are inconsistent as printed. Beyond this, loading N classical components into a shaped photon, preparing the read pulse, memory loss, detector efficiency, and the samples needed to estimate an overlap are not costed or benchmarked.

key_findings.claim: The link to Friston's free-energy principle is speculative and changes meanings of free energy across the argument.
key_findings.evidence: The paper moves from thermodynamic Helmholtz free energy of a switch to a prediction-error emulator and then asserts that the correct control policy minimizes change in the agent's free energy. No generative density, variational free-energy functional, Markov-blanket construction, or policy objective is derived, and no RL or active-inference experiment tests equivalence. Near-zero update work after learning follows for any converged update rule and does not select a policy by itself.

method.core_idea: Replace abstract nonlinear activations with noisy dissipative physical switches and analyze learning as stochastic control of their transition rates and physical bias parameters.
method.mechanism: The paper develops double-well and two-state Markov switches, continuous noisy observation, quantum-dot tunnelling, sampled-gradient NOT/XOR perceptrons, Ornstein-Uhlenbeck weight dynamics, Hopf-limit-cycle spiking elements, and a temporal-mode single-photon overlap detector. It then relates selected distributional changes to thermodynamic quantities and sketches an agent-centered free-energy interpretation.
assumptions: The physical switch rapidly reaches the steady state associated with each new input and weight setting.
Repeated samples give an accurate estimate of the activation probability before every update.
Phenomenological transition rates correspond to a thermodynamically consistent driven device.
Mean internal-energy and state-entropy changes can stand in for total work, heat, and entropy production.
Analytic gradients and feedback can be implemented without dominating the physical energy budget.
Simple logic-gate behavior predicts useful scaling to networks and realistic tasks.
Quantum state preparation, memory, control pulses, and readout do not erase the proposed kernel advantage.

techniques.role: Models a noisy binary activation through controllable transition rates.
Infers switch state from a filtered continuous noisy measurement.
Updates perceptron weights from repeated estimates of Bernoulli means.
Represents continuously adapting weights as stochastic dynamics in a learned potential.
Uses a tunable limit cycle whose phase noise trades against dissipated power.
Maps temporal-mode overlaps to single-photon detection probabilities.

evaluations.setting: Numerical overdamped double-well and two-state Markov switches.
evaluations.metric: Mean response, stochastic trajectories, first-passage behavior, and filtered conditional state.
evaluations.result: Illustrates the qualitative noise-speed-error trade-off expected of an activation switch.
evaluations.baseline: No calibrated physical device or alternative stochastic-switch model.

evaluations.setting: Simulated NOT perceptron with 200 switch samples per epoch and beta in {1, 0.1, 0.05}.
evaluations.result: The selected run converges faster for larger beta.
evaluations.baseline: Only beta variants; no deterministic perceptron, matched-cost learner, uncertainty, or held-out evaluation.

evaluations.setting: Two-hidden-unit simulated XOR network with fixed initial weights and 200 samples per trial.
evaluations.result: The displayed trace reaches low error for beta=1 and higher residual error for noisier settings.
evaluations.baseline: No seeds, exact-gradient check, conventional backpropagation control, or task scaling.

evaluations.setting: Analytic and simulated nonlinear oscillator/spiking primitives.
evaluations.metric: Limit-cycle phase diffusion, period variance, and thresholded integrated current.
evaluations.result: Increasing the cycle radius reduces timing noise while increasing dissipated power; chosen thresholds gate spiking.
evaluations.baseline: No trained SNN or energy-accuracy benchmark.

evaluations.metric: Detection probability proportional to a squared overlap.
evaluations.result: A formal overlap detector is proposed, but the stated data state is not normalized and no experiment or resource analysis is given.
evaluations.baseline: No classical kernel evaluator or end-to-end quantum resource count.

limitations: This is a broad theoretical perspective, not an experimental demonstration of a learning machine.
The thermodynamic accounting does not separate applied work, internal-energy change, heat, controller cost, sensing cost, and total entropy production.
Several central equations contain hazard, learning-rate, or normalization inconsistencies.
Only tiny NOT and XOR training examples are shown, with fixed favorable parameters and no uncertainty.
Repeated sampling and external gradient/feedback computation may dominate latency and energy but are excluded.
Quantum-dot and spiking sections do not train a fabricated device.
The single-photon kernel omits state-preparation, memory, detection, and sampling resources.
The free-energy-principle connection is asserted without a common objective or empirical test.
There is no comparison with physical self-learning, equilibrium propagation, reservoir computing, memristive training, or later thermodynamic-neuron implementations.
failure_modes: Low noise suppresses transitions and makes each activation estimate prohibitively slow.
High noise increases sample complexity enough to overwhelm device-level energy savings.
State-dependent hazards invalidate a simplified work distribution and derived identities.
External measurement and feedback dissipate more energy than the activation element.
Analog parameter drift and device mismatch prevent the assumed sigmoid response and analytic gradient.
Mean-field substitution in a stochastic multilayer network yields biased hidden-layer gradients.
Phase noise, synchronization, and fan-out make limit-cycle spiking networks unstable at scale.
Photon loss and O(1/epsilon-squared) sampling erase any overlap-evaluation advantage.
reusable_insights: Treat latency, error, and dissipated power as a joint frontier for every physical activation primitive.
Distinguish a single stochastic output from its ensemble activation curve and cost the samples needed to estimate the latter.
Measure the controller, sensing, conversion, reset, and communication energy in addition to device-core energy.
Use trajectory-level first-law bookkeeping and total entropy production rather than changes in mean state energy alone.
For oscillator neurons, phase diffusion provides a concrete reliability metric linked to drive power.
Audit quantum feature maps for normalization, state-loading complexity, loss, and shot complexity before claiming efficiency.
Validate analytic stochastic gradients against automatic differentiation and finite differences before mapping them into hardware.
open_questions: Can a fabricated noisy switch learn a nontrivial task with end-to-end joules and latency below matched CMOS and analog baselines?
What is the correct thermodynamic lower bound when sensing, memory, feedback, and resets are included?
How should transition rates be engineered so local detailed balance and desired activation curves hold simultaneously?
Can autonomous local physical dynamics implement multilayer credit assignment without digital gradients?
Which noise level minimizes total energy-to-accuracy after accounting for repeated sampling?
Do limit-cycle spiking networks retain the predicted phase-noise advantage under coupling, fan-out, and device disorder?
Can a normalized photonic feature map yield an end-to-end advantage after state preparation and measurement?
Is there a formal common objective relating thermodynamic free energy, variational free energy, and control policy selection?

competitive_landscape.title: Thermodynamic efficiency of learning a rule in neural networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Goldt and Seifert define learned information and thermodynamic cost in a stochastic teacher-student network and derive an efficiency bound for batch and online rules; the present paper adapts their setting to physical switches but offers a looser and internally inconsistent energy-error relation.

competitive_landscape.title: Thermodynamic Computing via Autonomous Quantum Thermal Machines
competitive_landscape.difference: Lipka-Bartosik et al. construct thermodynamically consistent qubit heat machines implementing NOT, majority, NOR, and networks with explicit steady-state dynamics and performance-dissipation trade-offs, making the quantum activation concept considerably more concrete.

competitive_landscape.title: Thermodynamic computing out of equilibrium
competitive_landscape.difference: Whitelam et al. train nonlinear Langevin circuits as universal approximators at finite observation times and test noise robustness; it more directly realizes computation powered by fluctuations, though it still relies on simulation and external genetic optimization.

competitive_landscape.title: Training all-mechanical neural networks for task learning through in situ backpropagation
competitive_landscape.difference: Li and Mao derive exact local physical gradients and provide experimental plus numerical validation on regression and classification, addressing multilayer credit assignment and retraining more directly than the paper's NOT/XOR simulations.

competitive_landscape.title: A self-learning magnetic Hopfield neural network with intrinsic gradient descent adaption
competitive_landscape.difference: Niu et al. demonstrate a spintronic network whose conductance evolves toward Oja learning under applied inputs, directly targeting autonomous in-material training rather than analytic external feedback.

competitive_landscape.title: Machine learning in and out of equilibrium
competitive_landscape.difference: Adhikari et al. derive Fokker-Planck currents, entropy production, and fluctuation theorems for stochastic-gradient dynamics and validate them on nonlinear regression and MNIST, providing the trajectory-level thermodynamic tests absent here.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Physical learning should be understood through stochastic dissipative switches; classical and quantum devices can exploit an optimal amount of noise, spiking limit cycles offer a tunable noise-power trade-off, and single photons may evaluate kernels at very low energy.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper unifies several illustrative stochastic models, derives sampled perceptron updates, visualizes NOT/XOR learning and oscillator phase diffusion, and maps quantum-dot and Raman-memory components onto activation and kernel language.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The synthesis is pedagogically broad and the activation-switch distinction is valuable, but the main thermodynamic result is not supported by correct heat/entropy accounting, several equations are inconsistent, and no physical learner or end-to-end advantage is demonstrated. Later thermodynamic-neuron and physical-self-learning work now provides more direct competitors and stronger validation targets.

reviewer_notes: Read all 43 extracted pages, including equations, acknowledgments, and references. Visually inspected the quantum-dot response, NOT/XOR learning curves, learned weight distribution, spiking threshold traces, and photon-kernel equations. Six primary arXiv/proceedings competitors were checked on 2026-08-23.
